title: Expanding Nanopatterned Substrates Using Stitch Technique for Nanotopographical Modulation of Cell Behavior
protocol: Replicate PDMS molds from an EBL mold.
Fabricate a silicon mold.
Spin coat 200 μl PMMA solution on a 1 × 1 cm silicon substrate at 2,500 rpm for 1 min to form a thin film.
Bake the PMMA film on the Si substrate at 180 °C for 2 min.
Write a designed nanopattern on the PMMA film using a focused electron beam at an area dose of 300 µC/cm².
Develop the PMMA nanopattern in developer for 80 sec.
Deposit a nickel layer of 50 nm thickness onto the PMMA nanopattern using an E-beam evaporator at an output voltage of 10 kV, emission current of 0.5 mA and deposition rate of 0.5 Å/sec.
Lift off the PMMA part in 20 ml remover at 80 °C for 20 min.

Reactive ion etch (RIE) the nanopattern into the Si substrate using a gas mixture of tetrafluoromethane (CF4)/oxygen (O2) (90%/10%) at an ICP power of 400 W and RIE power of 150 W to etch the Si substrate to a depth of 560 nm.
Silanize the Si mold.
Place a glass coverslip and the Si mold in a 100 mm PS Petri dish.
Drop 10 μl 1H,1H,2H,2H-Perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane on the coverslip.
Partially cover the Petri dish.
Keep the desiccator under vacuum for 5 hr in a fume hood to complete silanization of the Si mold.
Weigh 10 g of PDMS resin and 1.05 g of curing agent in a disposable weighing boat.
Mix the PDMS prepolymer thoroughly using a plastic spoon.
Degas the PDMS prepolymer in a plastic desiccator under vacuum for about 20 minutes until a clear mixture is observed.
Put the silanized Si mold in a 60 mm Petri dish.
Pour the degassed PDMS prepolymer onto the Si mold in the Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish in a plastic desiccator and degas again for about 10 minutes until all bubbles disappear.
Transfer the Petri dish to a hotplate and cure the PDMS prepolymer at 70 °C for 4 hours.
Peel off the cured PDMS mold from the Si mold carefully using tweezers.
Clean a Si substrate with ethanol in a fume hood and dry it with compressed air.
Trim off the unpatterned areas of each PDMS mold with a blade.
Place the trimmed PDMS mold with the nanopattern face-down on the mirror side of the Si substrate.
Align other molds close to but not touching the surrounding mold(s).
Cast 1 g degassed PDMS prepolymer (PDMS resin and curing agent ratio: 10:1.05) on a clean glass slide to form a 0.5 mm thick layer.
Bake the PDMS layer at 100 °C on a hotplate for 3-5 min.
Use a needle to touch the layer and ensure that the layer is partially but not completely cured.
Place the PDMS layer on the backside of aligned PDMS molds and quickly invert this assembly and transfer it to the hotplate.
Apply a compressive force (5 kPa) using a metal block on the top of assembly to ensure good contact between the PDMS adhesive layer and the backside of PDMS molds.
Cure the PDMS adhesive layer at 100 °C for 1 hr.
Remove the metal block.
Peel off the single, stitched PDMS mold from the Si substrate.
Dry PS pellets in a vacuum oven at 80°C for two days.
Preheat a press machine at 230°C.
Assemble an aluminum plate, PTFE sheet, and aluminum spacer from bottom to top.
Load 3.5 g PS pellets into the aluminum spacer with dimensions of 3 cm (L) × 3 cm (W) × 0.3 cm (H).
Place another PTFE sheet on top of the assembly followed by an aluminum plate.
Preheat the PS pellets at 230°C for 30 min in the press machine.
Apply a compressive pressure of 0.1 MPa on the assembly for 5 min.
Release the pressure and reapply with 0.5 MPa compressive pressure.
Increase pressure by 0.5 MPa increments until reaching 1.5 MPa.
Turn off the heater of the press machine when reaching 1.5 MPa.
Cool down to below 70°C while maintaining a constant pressure of 1.5 MPa.
Take the assembly out and store the PS plate in a vacuum oven at 80°C to prevent moisture from re-entering the PS plate.
Place the PS plate in an aluminum spacer set on a 3-inch Si wafer.
Heat the PS plate on a hotplate at 250°C for 30 min.
Put the stitched PDMS mold with nanopatterns face-down on the molten PS plate.
Apply a compressive pressure of 12.5 kPa using metal blocks on the aluminum plate and wait for 3 min.
Increase the compressive pressure to 25 kPa.
Repeat the step with the pressure increased to 50 kPa.
Maintain the temperature of the hotplate between 240°C and 250°C under a consistent pressure of 50 kPa for 15 min.
Turn off the hotplate and cool down the whole setup.
Dissolve 1 g PS in 10 ml toluene in a fume hood.
Spin-coat 1 ml PS solution on a 2-in wafer at 2,500 rpm for 1 min to form ~1 μm thick PS thin film.
Evaporate toluene from the film by setting the PS film on Si wafer in a fume hood for 3 days.
Anneal the PS thin film in a vacuum oven at 80 °C overnight.
Put the stitched PDMS mold with nanotopography face-down on the PS thin film, which is set on a hotplate.
Apply a compressive pressure of 12 kPa on the PDMS mold by using metal blocks on the glass side of the PDMS mold.
Increase the temperature of the hotplate to 180 °C and maintain it for 15 min.
Remove the metal blocks after the temperature drops below 50 °C.
Peel off the stitched PDMS mold from the PS film carefully.
Cast PDMS working substrates from the master mold generated in previous steps.
Cut the nanopatterned PDMS substrates into discs with a hollow steel arch punch to fit specific multi-well plates.
Use tweezers to place the PDMS discs into the wells of a multi-well plate.
Sterilize the PDMS substrates using 70% ethanol for 30 min.
Expose the PDMS substrates to UV light for 30 min.
Wash the PDMS substrates with 1x sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) three times.
Coat the PDMS substrates with extracellular matrix protein at a concentration of 20 μg/ml fibronectin for 30 min at room temperature.
Rinse the PDMS substrates with sterile PBS three times, each rinse lasting 5 min.
Suspend human lung cancer cell A549 in Dulbecco's modified eagle medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Plate the cells at a density of 2,000 cells/cm² on the PDMS substrates.
Culture the plated cells at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO₂ for one day.
Wash the cells with PBS three times.
Fix cells in a mixture of 4% paraformaldehyde and 2% glutaraldehyde in PBS for 4 hours.
Dehydrate cells using a CO2 critical point dryer for scanning electronic microscopic observation.
